analysis: Cross-source read: the tape opened softer than the flat futures suggested, and the reason is a double repricing — rates and oil both ticked up into the bell. The 10Y touching 5% and Brent back over $100 (Trump's 'annihilate' threat unwinding the Iran-diplomacy peace premium) flipped yesterday's disinflation tailwind into today's mild headwind; the Nasdaq, coming off its second straight record close, is digesting on the way down. What changed vs the 6:04 AM PT premarket brief: (1) post-open price action is in — Dow/S&P -0.1-0.2%, Nasdaq -0.2-0.3%, META +1.5% is the lone Mag-7 bright spot; (2) September flash PMIs printed cooler but intact — composite 53.6 (Aug 54.6), services 53.9, mfg 52.0 — and Williamson still reads Q3 GDP at a 2.2% annualized pace, 'best quarter of the year,' so the softening is a sentiment/hiring slowdown, not a contraction; (3) the Meta Connect pre-game crystallized — camera-free 'Luna' glasses per The Information (single-source), Muse #1 on the App Store for five straight days per Sensor Tower (Barron's), +20% since launch, Wells Fargo to $796; (4) the AI-supply-chain rotation continues: memory names digesting post-breakout while quantum (IONQ catalyst) was this morning's speculative offset. Signal: flash-PMI resilience with cooler hiring, Connect keynote tonight, oil/Brent>$100. Noise: AppLovin -5%/Booking -4% are un-headlined early moves; the Luna glasses report is single-source until Zuckerberg says it.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Indexes opened lower: Nasdaq -0.2%, Dow -0.1%, S&P 500 -0.1% at the bell; just after the open IBD had Dow -0.2%, S&P -0.2%, Nasdaq -0.3%, SPY -0.2%, QQQ -0.4% (Investopedia, IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Record-chase profit-taking plus 10Y at 5% and Brent >$100 pressure early bids — the open is about Connect tonight and PMI digestion, not new macro.

headlines.headline: Flash US September PMIs came in cool-but-expanding: composite 53.6 (Aug 54.6), services 53.9 (prior 54.5, ~in line), manufacturing 52.0 (prior 53.0, in line). S&P Global's Williamson reads the data as a 2.2% annualized Q3 GDP pace — 'best quarter of the year' — but flags hiring pullback, tariff-driven input costs, and an 'unprecedented' manufacturing inventory build-up (investinglive, FXStreet).
headlines.why_it_matters: Soft-landing intact with cooler hiring — supports the view that rates can ease eventually, but the margin-squeeze/inventory notes are deflationary whispers for cyclicals.

headlines.headline: Eurozone composite PMI surprised to 53.1 in September (est. 51.7), the fastest expansion since April 2023; services bounced to 53.0 and Germany hit 53.8 composite (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Transatlantic resilience reduces global-recession tail risk, though rising energy-driven input costs keep the ECB hawkish — net: growth ok, cuts not coming.

headlines.headline: META +1.5% at the open ahead of tonight's 7pm ET Connect keynote; Barron's reports Muse has been the #1 free iOS app for five straight days (Sensor Tower) and shares are +20% since the Sept 8 launch. Reuters/The Information (single-source) say Meta will unveil camera-free 'Luna' smart glasses, a new camera Ray-Ban, and the thinner 'Phoenix' AR device.
headlines.why_it_matters: The lone Mag-7 gainer — engagement data and hardware reveals tonight can either cement the ~20% Muse rerate or trigger 'sell the news'.
